claims.text: Public Law 119-60 (FY2026 NDAA, approved 18 December 2025), Div. A, Title XVI, secs. 1671-1673, 139 Stat. 1201-1203: sec. 1671 'Briefings on intercepts of unidentified anomalous phenomena by North American Aerospace Defense Command and United States Northern Command'; sec. 1672 'Elimination of duplicative reporting requirements relating to unidentified anomalous phenomena'; sec. 1673 'Accounting of security classification guides relating to unidentified anomalous phenomena'.
Sec. 1671(b) requires the first post-enactment briefing to cover NORAD/USNORTHCOM UAP intercepts 'not previously provided that occurred during the period beginning on January 1, 2004'.

Sec. 1672(a) repeals 50 U.S.C. 3373a (sec. 413 of the IAA for FY2022); sec. 1672(b) rewrites 50 U.S.C. 3373(f)(1)(A) and adds the new qualifier 'in a manner that protects intelligence sources and methods' to the immediate-data-availability mandate.

Sec. 1673(a) requires the Director of AARO within 180 days to account for 'security classification guides that apply to information used for reports and investigations of unidentified anomalous phenomena' and permits a 'consolidated security classification matrix for programs relating to unidentified anomalous phenomena'.

The FY2026 NDAA requires AARO to brief lawmakers on UAP intercepts by NORAD and U.S. Northern Command dating back to 2004, including 'the number, location, and nature' of intercepts and 'data collected or analyzed during such intercepts.'
AARO must account for 'UAP-related security classification guides' used in reports and investigations, addressing overclassification and improper restrictions on releasing imagery or data.

Disclosure Foundation executive director Jordan Flowers called the provisions 'a meaningful, if incremental, step toward transparency and oversight,' noting two mirror recommendations championed by Christopher Mellon.

The conferenced FY2026 NDAA requires the AARO Director to brief Congress on operations since 2004 involving UAP intercepts by NORAD and US Northern Command, including the 'number, location, and nature' of intercepts and 'procedures and protocols followed during those operations, including any data collected or analyzed during such intercepts.'

A second provision requires AARO to account for UAP-related security classification guides affecting 'reports and investigations of such phenomena'; a third eliminates duplicative reporting requirements and streamlines agency data-sharing with AARO.
The provisions reflect recommendations from Christopher Mellon and the Disclosure Foundation.

claims.source: DefenseScoop, 10 December 2025, on the FY2026 NDAA UAP provisions
claims.text: The FY2026 NDAA requires AARO to brief Congress on UAP intercepts by NORAD and USNORTHCOM since 2004, including number, location, nature, procedures, protocols and data collected.
The FY2026 NDAA requires AARO to account for the UAP-related security classification guides used in its reports and investigations.
The FY2026 NDAA streamlines federal agency data sharing with the Pentagon for AARO investigations and eliminates duplicative reporting requirements.
The NDAA FY2026 (P.L. 119-60) was approved 18 December 2025.

Section 1672 repeals section 413 of the Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2022 (50 U.S.C. 3373a) and amends 50 U.S.C. 3373(f)(1)(A) to require IC elements and DoD components with UAP data to make it available to AARO immediately.

Section 1673 directs the AARO Director, not later than 180 days after enactment, to make an accounting of security classification guides applying to UAP reports and investigations, and permits a consolidated security classification matrix.
Section 1671 requires briefings on intercepts of UAP by North American Aerospace Defense Command and United States Northern Command.

Neither the FY2025 NDAA (P.L. 118-159) nor the FY2026 NDAA (P.L. 119-60) re-enacted the section 1687(a) prohibition on funding unreported UAP special access activity; a full-text search of both Acts returns no instance of the phrase 'restricted access limitation'.
Section 6802 of the FY2025 NDAA sunsets the audit and reporting requirements relating to the UAP Historical Record Report, tying them to 90 and 180 days after delivery of the final volume.

desc: The National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026 was approved on 18 December 2025. Its UAP provisions run in two opposite directions at once and both matter to the money question. Section 1672, 'Elimination of Duplicative Reporting Requirements Relating to Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena', repeals section 413 of the Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2022 (50 U.S.C. 3373a) outright, and rewrites section 1683(f)(1)(A) of the FY2022 NDAA so that the DNI and the Secretary of Defense 'shall jointly require that each element of the intelligence community and component of the Department of Defense with data relating to unidentified anomalous phenomena makes such data available immediately to the Office in a manner that protects intelligence sources and methods.' Section 1673, 'Accounting of Security Classification Guides Relating to Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena', directs the Director of AARO within 180 days of enactment - by roughly 16 June 2026 - to make an accounting of the security classification guides that apply to information used for UAP reports and investigations, and permits issuance of a consolidated security classification matrix. Section 1671 requires briefings on intercepts of UAP by NORAD and USNORTHCOM. What is absent is as important as what is present: neither the FY2025 nor the FY2026 NDAA re-enacted the section 1687(a) bar on funds for unreported UAP special access activity, which by its terms applied only to funds authorised by the FY2024 Act. The permanent piece - the IR&D indirect-cost prohibition at section 1687(b), codified as a 50 U.S.C. 3373 note - survives; the annual funding bar did not.

timeline.text: Section 6802 of the FY2025 NDAA ties the quarterly and semiannual audit and reporting requirements on the UAP Historical Record Report to 90 and 180 days after delivery of the final volume. The same Act does not re-enact the section 1687(a) funding bar, which lapsed with fiscal year 2024.
